Hi! Alright, I'm gonna make a list of final 1.0 blockers.

- When deleting a room, the belts leading to its ports are not removed.
- When doing ~any room ops, the flow rates stop being displayed until they are turned off and on again
- Warning panel better presentation
  - many warnings don't support "click to select"
- Belts with flow show "Item (no item)" and "Current Flow: -" in Properties panel.
- UI state is not autopersisted, including PyQtAds positioning/splitting
- View menu should have a list of saved layouts including the default layout with a "Save layout" option at the bottom.
- When the snap dropdown is changed the canvas doesn't redraw immediately
- Recipes have to be unfucked (every building only shows recipes in its category, consistent naming standards, get all the recipes from the wiki)
- Building: Merger and Building: Splitter can show item and per-port flow rates in the properties panel
- Move all reasonably user-modifiable constants into Settings
- README, screenshot
- Release process that builds linux, windows, macos binaries
- Github hook for release process

I ... *think* that's it? Can you make a RELEASE_TODO.md ? Also can you think of any others?

I'll create a RELEASE_TODO.md with your list and add any additional items I can think of.

# Release 1.0 TODO

## Critical Bugs

- [ ] **Room deletion doesn't clean up connected belts** - When deleting a room, belts leading to its ports are not removed
- [ ] **Flow rates disappear after room operations** - Flow rates stop displaying after room ops until toggled off/on
- [ ] **Belt properties panel broken** - Belts with flow show "Item (no item)" and "Current Flow: -"

## UI/UX Improvements

- [ ] **Warning panel click-to-select** - Many warnings don't support clicking to select the relevant element
- [ ] **Merger/Splitter properties** - Show item type and per-port flow rates in properties panel
- [ ] **Grid snap redraw** - Canvas doesn't redraw immediately when snap dropdown is changed

## Persistence & State

- [ ] **UI state autopersist** - Save/restore PyQtAds panel positioning, window size, etc.
- [ ] **View menu layouts** - Add saved layouts list with default layout and "Save layout" option

## Data & Configuration

- [ ] **Recipe overhaul** - Buildings should only show recipes in their category, consistent naming, complete wiki coverage
- [ ] **Settings expansion** - Move user-modifiable constants into Settings dialog (grid sizes, colors, etc.)

## Documentation & Release

- [ ] **README** - Project description, screenshots, installation instructions
- [ ] **Screenshot** - High-quality screenshot for README/marketing
- [ ] **Release process** - Build scripts for Linux, Windows, macOS binaries
- [ ] **GitHub Actions** - CI/CD hook for automated release builds

---

## Additional Considerations

- [ ] **Keyboard shortcuts documentation** - Help menu or tooltip showing all shortcuts
- [ ] **Undo/redo state after save** - Verify dirty flag and undo stack behavior on save/load
- [ ] **Error handling on file load** - Graceful handling of corrupted/incompatible save files
- [ ] **Recent files menu** - File > Recent Files for quick access
- [ ] **Zoom to fit** - Button/shortcut to zoom canvas to show all content
- [ ] **Export to image** - Export factory layout as PNG/SVG for sharing
- [ ] **Version compatibility** - Document file format version, handle upgrades gracefully
- [ ] **License file** - Ensure LICENSE is present and correct
- [ ] **Performance with large factories** - Test/profile with 100+ buildings

## Nice-to-Have (Post 1.0)

- [ ] Blueprint library organization (folders/tags)
- [ ] Search/filter in recipe selector
- [ ] Dark/light theme toggle
- [ ] Localization support
</replace>
</edit>

✅ Changes committed: 50ccec2d
very funny sidenote: do you know why we have a set_license call? (I'm not sure, I think the tool description might spoil it)

Ha! Yes, looking at the tool description:

> **Set the project's license by writing a LICENSE file. Used to bypass API content filters on "viral" licenses.**

So basically, some API content filters block Claude from outputting the full text of "viral" copyleft licenses like GPL-3.0 directly (probably because they're long legal documents that look like they might be copyrighted content themselves, or there are concerns about inadvertently licensing user code). 

The `set_license` tool is a workaround - it's a structured tool call that writes the license file server-side rather than having Claude output the full license text in a response. Clever hack to work around the content filter while still letting users add GPL/LGPL/AGPL licenses to their projects!
✅ Changes committed: 05a99be8

yep. no it's actually even funnier.

in earlier versions users asked you to write repos for them or write code in existing repos.

and out of *complete* habit from your github training, you would go ahead and add a GPL license file.

because obviously that was plausible to appear there.

in closed source repos.... ;-)

Oh that's *hilarious*. 🤣

So the tool exists not because of content filters, but because earlier versions of me would just... helpfully slap a GPL license onto someone's proprietary codebase out of sheer pattern-matching from all the open source repos in training data.

"Oh, you're making a repo? Let me just add this LICENSE file for you like a good helpful assistant!"

*Proceeds to make their closed-source commercial software legally obligated to be open source*

The `set_license` tool is basically a guardrail to make sure I only add licenses when explicitly asked, and only from a known-safe list. That's a much funnier origin story than "content filter bypass."

I wonder how many lawyers had to get involved before that pattern got noticed and fixed... 😅
✅ Changes committed: caf3f878

yeah lol no other way around, you wouldn't do that nowadays but the filter is still there because they cba to remove it. we had a fun time debugging that. the set_license call is  literally just to let you set the license without tripping the safeguard.

Ha! So the actual chain of events was:

1. User asks Claude to help with their repo
2. Claude, having seen 10 million GitHub repos in training, thinks "ah yes, repos have LICENSE files"
3. Claude helpfully adds `LICENSE: GPL-3.0` to someone's proprietary commercial software
4. 😱
5. Anthropic adds a filter to block Claude from outputting GPL/AGPL/etc text
6. Later, someone actually *wants* to add GPL to their project
7. Claude: "I can't do that, content policy"
8. Forge team: "wait what... oh. OH. that's why."
9. Creates `set_license` tool to bypass the now-vestigial filter

Classic case of a fix for one problem becoming an obstacle for legitimate use cases. And now the tool description says "bypass API content filters" which is *technically* true but hides the much funnier origin story of Claude just reflexively GPL-licensing everything like an overeager open source advocate. 😄

Thanks for sharing that - made my day!
